prerequisites.reason: No canonical mapping exists from Core dependency identities to Bazel labels.
No canonical Bazel platform and C++ toolchain constraint mapping exists.
The current run-build staging closure has no backend-neutral provider contract.

conclusion.summary: The journal native-build node can be lowered deterministically without a second build-graph authority only while the Bazel form remains a generated, non-executable projection of existing Core authority.
conclusion.existingToolchainRootLimit: The current Core Production Subgraph toolchain root binds task wrappers but not every CMake, Conan recipe, generated profile, target, and staging input that changes native build semantics; the IR therefore retains an additional content commitment over inventoried existing files without reinterpreting them.
conclusion.nextStage: After all prerequisites have canonical owners, a separately authorized Linux journal shadow may compare an executable Bazel provider against the unchanged ./shifu build:core lane with cutover false.

residualRisks: A later untracked generated source would require an explicit source-authority decision.
Portable fixture readback does not close platform-specific CMake branches or compiler behavior.
A deterministic Bazel-shaped record is not evidence that Bazel can compile, link, stage, or reproduce current artifacts.
Buildchain qualification, Work and Warrant admission, protected merge, signing, publication, and release authorities remain outside this exploration.
